title: Gayle Rankin Breaks Down That Shocking Aemond Dream Scene in House of the Dragon Episode 7
excerpt: The actress behind Alys Rivers discusses the 'absurd' Aemond-Alicent-Alys sex dream, reveals real-life friendship with Olivia Cooke made filming even wilder, and teases her character's dragon egg plans at Harrenhal.
body:
• Gayle Rankin called filming the Aemond-Alicent-Alys dream sequence "a pretty crazy f***ing scene" and said her real-life friendship with Olivia Cooke added to the absurdity.
  • Episode 7 revealed Dreamfyre for the first time in the series and brought back Sunfyre, Aegon's dragon presumed dead since the Battle of Rook's Rest.
  • Alys Rivers keeps a clutch of five dragon eggs at Harrenhal, hatched by Dreamfyre, positioning her as a key player ahead of the season finale.
  • Alicent Hightower arrives at Harrenhal on a mission from Rhaenyra to assassinate her own son Aemond, setting up a pivotal finale confrontation.

House of the Dragon Season 3 Episode 7 delivered one of the show's most talked-about sequences yet — a hallucinatory dream in which Aemond Targaryen (Ewan Mitchell) believes he is having sex with his mother Alicent Hightower (Olivia Cooke), only for the scene to reveal he is actually sleeping with Alys Rivers (Gayle Rankin). In a new interview with Decider, Rankin opened up about the surreal filming experience and what it means for her character going forward.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=LQXyHAzZ_9o

The Dream Scene That Nobody Could Talk About

The sequence begins with a shirtless Aemond practicing his swordplay at Harrenhal when Alicent appears, claiming she has fled King's Landing to be with him. As they begin having sex on the weirwood bed, the vision peels away to show Aemond is actually with Alys — his Oedipal fixation playing out in one of Harrenhal's signature hallucinatory episodes.

"Shooting it was the thing that we couldn't talk about in the junket," Rankin told Decider with a chuckle. "People were like, 'What was the craziest scene you had to shoot?' I think that was a pretty crazy f***ing scene, for all of us."

"It was fun and funny. Those scenes can sometimes be really intense, but they're also ultimately stunt scenes in some ways. We all just try to be really respectful and professional and keep it pretty lighthearted. Because it was a very absurd scene."

— Gayle Rankin, Actress (Alys Rivers)

Rankin revealed that her real-life friendship with Olivia Cooke heightened the strangeness of the shoot. She also confirmed the episode marks the first time Aemond and Alys consummate their relationship. "We're seeing it happen in front of our eyes," she said. "It's early days of that endeavor, so it's vulnerable still, I think, for them."

Dragons Emerge: Dreamfyre and Sunfyre Shake Up the War

Beyond the Aemond dream, Episode 7 delivered two major dragon revelations. For the first time in the show's run, viewers saw Dreamfyre, the she-dragon bonded to Helaena Targaryen (Phia Saban). Director Nina Lopez-Corrado told Entertainment Weekly the sequence involved Helaena envisioning herself mounting Dreamfyre in the Dragonpit and torching an army of smallfolk — a nightmarish vision that reinforces her fear of dragonriding's corrupting power.

"She thinks that dragons change people and that they've changed their whole world," Lopez-Corrado said. "She knows that deep down inside, because she is a Targaryen, there almost is no positive outcome to anything that's happening."

Meanwhile, Sunfyre — Aegon's (Tom Glynn-Carney) mount presumed dead after the Battle of Rook's Rest in Season 2 — returned to defend his rider in the woods. Dragon and dragonrider now bear mirrored scars on the same side of their faces. "I think it 100 percent has to do with the Targaryen line and the connection they have with the dragons," Lopez-Corrado said of Sunfyre's reemergence.

Alys Rivers and the Harrenhal Dragon Eggs

Alys's role has expanded well beyond Harrenhal's resident witch. Previous episodes revealed she possesses a clutch of five dragon eggs at the cursed castle, hatched by Dreamfyre. With Aemond now under her influence and the eggs in her care, Alys is emerging as one of the war's most unpredictable power players.

Rankin has previously described her character's arc this season as "more personal," telling The Times that Season 3 takes Alys on "big journeys." By episode's end, Alys is calling Aemond an "idiot" for allowing himself to be poisoned by his own mother — a dynamic that suggests her hold over the one-eyed prince is tightening.

What's Next: Alicent's Mission and the Finale

The episode's other major thread sees Alicent arriving at Harrenhal not as a fleeing mother, but as an assassin. Rhaenyra (Emma D'Arcy) has charged her former rival with killing Aemond — Alicent's own son — a mission that sets up the season's most emotionally charged finale confrontation.

Elsewhere, Lord Ormund Hightower (James Norton) courts Ulf the White (Tom Bennett), promising him the Driftmark throne in exchange for betraying Rhaenyra. Lopez-Corrado advised viewers to "start refreshing your memories for the Battle of Tumbleton," suggesting the finale will deviate from George R.R. Martin's Fire & Blood source material in significant ways.

The House of the Dragon Season 3 finale airs on HBO and streams on Max on Sunday, August 9 at 9 PM ET.
